usage: Use 菊花 to talk about the chrysanthemum as a flower, especially in gardening, flower markets, and plant-related conversations.
It is a very common everyday noun, so it fits naturally after numbers, colors, and adjectives when describing different kinds of flowers.
In Hong Kong, 菊花 is often associated with autumn and with festival or offering contexts, so the tone can sometimes feel a bit cultural or seasonal.
Learners can use it as a simple countable noun when naming the plant itself, or in phrases about buying, growing, or admiring flowers.
